destination.name: Cooktown
destination.tagline: A frontier port where Captain Cook beached the Endeavour, gateway to Cape York
destination.description: Cooktown is a small coastal town on the Endeavour River estuary, where Captain Cook beached his ship for 48 days in 1770. A century later it was the port for the Palmer River goldfields, and grand buildings were built in that boom. The town has a frontier feel, far from the resort towns further south. Grassy Hill and rainforest sit around it, and it is the base for travel north into Cape York.
whyVisit: Climb Grassy Hill for sweeping views

goodToKnow.title: Crocodiles and stingers
goodToKnow.detail: Crocodiles have been sighted at Finch Bay and Cherry Tree Bay, and stingers are present in season. Do not wade in creeks or the sea.

goodToKnow.title: Wet season flooding
goodToKnow.detail: Flooding has cut the town off in the wet. Check road conditions before driving and never cross a flooded creek.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}, the dry season, for warm, less humid days. The wet season runs December to April.
